name: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers and a target, return the 0-based indices `(i, j)` (with `i < j`) of two distinct elements whose sum equals the target.

Each test case is one line on stdin in the form `target a_1 a_2 ... a_n`, where `target` is the desired sum and `a_1..a_n` is the array. The wrapper parses the line into a single integer array (`target` followed by the array elements) and calls `solve(nums)` with that array; your job is only to extract `target = nums[0]` and search inside `nums[1:]`. The judge runs each test case independently — your function handles one line at a time.

Return an array `[i, j]`; the wrapper serializes it as `"i j"`. Every test case has exactly one valid answer.
output_format: Two 0-based indices `i j` (separated by one space) into the array part of the input such that `array[i] + array[j] == target`, with `i < j`.
hints: Use a hash map: as you scan `nums[1:]`, check whether `target - x` was seen earlier.
Indices are 0-based into the array (i.e. into `nums[1:]`), and the smaller index comes first.
Values can be negative and up to ~1e9; prefer 64-bit integers in C++/Go.
